entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Feliks Kazimierz Potocki (1630–1702) was a Polish noble, magnate, and military leader.

As a key figure in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Potocki played a crucial role in the Great Northern War, leading the Polish forces against the Swedish Empire.

The Treaty of Vienna (1701) marked a significant victory for Potocki, securing the border between Poland and Sweden for decades to come.

Despite his military successes, Potocki's legacy was marred by the devastating consequences of the Great Northern War, which led to the decline of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Feliks Kazimierz Potocki's contributions to Polish military history remain an important topic of study among historians.

As a testament to his military prowess, Potocki's name is still revered in Poland today, with the Feliks Potocki Monument in Warsaw serving as a lasting tribute to his legacy.
